pll1d12c1-d1e3477.summary: Raises the question whether the Spirit proceeded from the Father before or more than from the Son, with a heretic's dilemma: either the Son was already born and his birth preceded the procession, or he was not and the procession preceded the birth.

pll1d12c1-d1e3480.summary: Answers with De Trinitate XV that such questions are more laborious than fruitful: in the Trinity there are no intervals of time, so one cannot ask whether the Spirit had proceeded when the Son was born. Whoever understands the Son's timeless generation should understand the Spirit's timeless procession from both.
claims: There are no time intervals in the Trinity.
Questions of temporal order cannot be asked of the eternal processions.
The Spirit's procession from both is timeless, like the Son's generation.

pll1d12c1-d1e3510.summary: Declares the question of prior procession from the Father solved.
claims: The question of priority is resolved.

pl-l1d12c1.summary: Addresses whether the Spirit proceeded from the Father before proceeding from the Son, against a heretical dilemma (either the Son was already born, so his birth preceded the procession, or not, so the procession preceded the birth). With Augustine, Lombard calls such questions more laborious than fruitful: in the Trinity there are no intervals of time, and whoever understands the timeless generation of the Son should understand the timeless procession of the Spirit from both.
claims: The Spirit did not proceed from the Father before proceeding from the Son.
There are no temporal intervals in the Trinity.
The procession of the Spirit is timeless, like the generation of the Son.
